subject: On‑prem commercial offer, migration credit and rollout tranche
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@summitdx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On‑prem commercial offer, migration credit and rollout tranche

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As promised, attached is a concise commercial outline for Summit Diagnostics' on‑prem (customer‑managed VPC) deployment. Key points up front:

- Perpetual vs term: we recommend a 3‑year term license (term licensing simplifies upgrades and support).
- License pricing: node‑based license (3 nodes initial) with optional burst nodes.
- Platform fee: annual platform fee for the private control plane; we can amortize the first‑year platform fee across the first 12 or 36 months per your accounting preference.
- Migration assistance: we can offer a one‑time migration credit to cover engineering hours for data transfer and onboarding.
- Support tiers: Standard (business hours), Premium (24/7 oncall + 1‑hour P1), Elite (dedicated TAM + monthly QBR).

Attached: Summit_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW stub), redwood_onprem_price_model.xlsx (pricing scenarios), and data_residency_addendum.docx.

A few optional concessions we can discuss: a migration credit of up to $150k for a 24‑month minimum commitment, or $250k for a 36‑month commitment; and a 10–15% license discount band tied to commit length and prepay. I want to be clear on the mechanics: migration credits are applied as service credits against the first invoice schedule (not as cash rebates), and platform fee amortization will be reflected in the invoice schedule we generate for your procurement team.

Could you confirm if Summit prefers capex (PO + invoice) or opex (monthly invoices)? Also, do you have any constraints around amortizing the platform fee?

If it helps, we can schedule a 30‑minute procurement call tomorrow to walk through the workbook.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555‑0192

--- Attachment stubs: Summit_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf), redwood_onprem_price_model.xlsx (xlsx), data_residency_addendum.docx (docx)

From: Daniel Park <dpark@summitdx.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@summitdx.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem commercial offer, migration credit and rollout tranche

Irene —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few follow ups from procurement & infra: 

1) We prefer capex (PO + net30 invoices) from an accounting perspective.
2) Can you clarify how the platform fee amortization looks on the invoice schedule? Procurement wants to avoid a one‑time large platform fee hitting this fiscal quarter if possible.
3) On migration credit — our migration windows are Q4 (Nov) and Q1 (Jan). Is the credit time‑boxed, or can we apply it to professional services within the first six months of contract start?
4) Support SLAs — we need written response times and credit language (SLA credits are common). If you can provide an SLA tranche table (P1, P2, P3 response/resolve times + credits) that would help.

Finally: can you provide a firm license discount if we commit to 36 months and prepay 80%? Procurement would treat that favorably.

Thanks — Daniel
Daniel Park
Head of IT Infrastructure, Summit Diagnostics

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 11:24:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: On‑prem commercial offer, migration credit and rollout tranche

Team — FYI; Procurement at Summit wants: capex billing, platform fee amortization schedule, migration credit timing, and a firm discount for 36 months w/ 80% prepay. Also asking for SLA credit language.

Quick asks:
- Ben, can you produce a 36‑month prepay scenario in the workbook with an amortized platform fee (show annual line items) and run the unit economics for the 3‑node starter + 10% burst?
- Grace, can you draft a short SLA tranche table we can include in the SOW (response times + credit % per severity)?
- Marissa, what's the negotiation room on license discount for 36‑month, 80% prepay and a migration credit ask of $250k? I want a recommended counter to present to Daniel if needed.

I'll loop back with a combined email to Summit once we have numbers.

Thanks — Irene

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 14:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: On‑prem commercial offer, migration credit and rollout tranche

Irene / team —

I updated the pricing workbook (see attached stub). Summary of recommended commercial counter:

- Commit options (license discount shown):
  * 12 months, monthly invoicing: 5% license discount, $0 migration credit
  * 24 months, 60% prepay: 10% license discount, $150k migration credit
  * 36 months, 80% prepay: 15% license discount, $250k migration credit

- Platform fee amortization: we can split the first‑year platform fee into 12 equal monthly invoices or amortize over contract term (12/24/36 months); for capex preference, we can present an invoice schedule that shows the platform fee as line items allocated to fiscal quarters to reduce quarter‑end impact (legal needs to agree).

- SLA tranches (draft):
  * P1: initial response 15 minutes; target restore 4 hours; SLA credit = 10% of monthly platform fee if missed
  * P2: initial response 1 hour; target restore 24 hours; SLA credit = 5% of monthly platform fee if missed
  * P3: initial response 4 hours; target restore 5 business days; SLA credit = 1% of monthly platform fee if missed

- Additional items: data residency addendum included to capture your on‑prem encryption/KMS needs; airgap installer available as a paid option.

I attached the redwood_onprem_price_model.xlsx (stub) and a short example invoice schedule. If Marissa confirms the 15% for 36‑month is approved, I recommend we present the 36‑month scenario to accelerate close and secure the migration credit.

—Ben

--- Attachment stubs: redwood_onprem_price_model.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <dpark@summitdx.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@summitdx.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Grace Oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 15:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On‑prem commercial offer, migration credit and rollout tranche

Daniel —

Appreciate the clarity on capex. Based on your asks, here is a concrete offer from Redwood: 

Offer (best commercial & implementation path):
- Term: 36 months
- License: node‑based, initial 3 nodes (expandable), 15% license discount conditional on 80% prepay at contract signature
- Migration credit: $250,000 applied as service credit against the first invoice(s); credit valid for professional services performed within the first six months after contract effective date
- Platform fee: present as a single line on the SOW but amortized across the invoice schedule per your preference; because you prefer capex, we will provide a quarterly invoice schedule that distributes the platform fee to avoid a one‑time large hit in Q3 (legal & finance review required)
- SLA tranches: attached table (P1/P2/P3) with credit percentages as discussed. Formal SLA language will be included in the SOW addendum.
- Data residency & KMS: addendum attached; airgapped installer available at additional cost.

Next steps to finalize:
1) I’ll send an updated SOW and invoice schedule (redlined) by EOD tomorrow.
2) If acceptable, Procurement can issue a PO referencing SUMMIT-2026-Q3-01 and the SOW.
3) Target kickoff: production rollout window Nov 2026 (we’ll align the migration window during onboarding).

Would you like me to share this offer as a clean PDF for your procurement review, or would you prefer a tracked SOW for legal redlines?

Cheers,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555‑0192

--- Attachment stubs: Summit_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf), data_residency_addendum.docx (docx), redwood_onprem_price_model.xlsx (xlsx)
